title: 2026 UK ETS sustainable-aviation-fuel current-rule versus consultation QA controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: Treatment of sustainable aviation fuel
UK Emissions Trading Scheme for aviation: how to comply

facts.source_fact: Aircraft operators purchasing eligible SAF can make an emissions reduction claim that can reduce their UK ETS aviation-emissions figure and corresponding surrender requirement.
facts.expected_handling: Treat a successful ERC as a current compliance mechanism.

facts.source_fact: The 2026 consultation describes current UK ETS eligible SAF as biogenic biofuel meeting the existing sustainability criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Do not apply proposed expanded fuel eligibility as current law.

facts.source_fact: The consultation describes the current UK ETS GHG savings threshold as 65 percent, or 55 percent for specified older production plants.
The consultation describes the current fossil-fuel comparator as 94 gCO2e per MJ.
facts.expected_handling: Do not substitute proposed comparator values.

facts.source_fact: Eligible SAF is currently zero-rated in the UK ETS when claim requirements are met.
facts.expected_handling: Apply zero rating only to an accepted eligible claim.

facts.source_fact: Current aviation guidance requires eligible fuel, timing and delivery conditions, no double benefit, and verification for an emissions reduction claim.
The March 2026 document is a consultation on future SAF treatment, not a government response implementing new rules.
facts.expected_handling: Label consultation options as proposals only.

facts.source_fact: The consultation considers expanding eligible SAF beyond biofuels and aligning eligibility with SAF Mandate criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat expanded eligibility as current rule.

facts.source_fact: The consultation considers continued zero rating versus lifecycle-based recognition of actual emissions savings.
facts.expected_handling: Keep policy options distinct from current zero rating.

facts.source_fact: The consultation states that the no-double-claiming requirement would be retained in contemplated operational changes.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve anti-double-count control in both current and proposed treatments.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve aviation guidance and consultation facts.
Separate current law from consultation options.
Check current eligible fuel and sustainability conditions.
Version savings threshold and fossil comparator.
Require timing, delivery, verification and no-double-benefit evidence.
Apply zero rating only after valid ERC.
Treat lifecycle recognition as a policy option unless implemented.
Bind policy status to publication and response state.
Do not infer parcel emissions from aviation fuel policy.
Flag conflicts between current ERC rules and proposed options.
